analysis.title: The Ghosts of Crises Past to Haunt the Midterms (Across the Americas)
key_insights: The FOMC held the policy rate at an upper bound of 4.0% in October, after a hike in September. Natixis says a December hike is now likely a foregone conclusion absent a significant data shift or a substantial tightening of financial conditions.

Chair Warsh's prepared remarks outlined a plan to keep eight FOMC meetings per year. At least one would be devoted to monetary policy strategy, with no vote or statement, and the rest would set policy.

September headline PCE rose 0.5% m/m and 3.6% y/y (from 0.3% and 3.4%). Core PCE rose 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y (from 3.0%), in line with expectations. The last two prints were noticeably hotter after cool summer numbers.

The personal savings rate fell to 3.8%, the lowest since Oct 2022. Incomes have diminished and consumers are drawing on savings. Natixis expects weak confidence, job prospects and wage growth to weigh on spending.

The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index rose 7.5 points to 91.7 in October. The Expectations Index rose to 72.6 and the Present Situation Index to 120.4. Consumers planned less spending on durable goods and services, so the rebound may not lift consumption. Gasoline prices were still up over 34% y/y.

September durable goods orders rose 1.8% m/m, a touch below expectations. Core capital goods orders rose 0.5% and shipments rose 1.2% against an expected 0.8%, which Natixis reads as resilient capital investment.
October payrolls are due Friday, with consensus at +55k after September's 29k, and the unemployment rate expected to stay at 4.2%. ISM Manufacturing, JOLTS and ISM Services are also due next week.

Midterms: Trump's approval is around 38%, and the president's party has lost an average of 25 House seats in post-WWII midterms. Prediction markets favor Democrats taking the House, and the Senate is harder but possible.

Rates strategy: the FOMC and core PCE added little new information. The rally in Treasuries was supported by AI/tech weakness and the ECB and Warsh pointing to tighter financial conditions. Natixis keeps its long 2yr UST trade and lowers the stop from 5.04% to 4.86%.

Natixis now sees medium-term risks to the long end as favorable. It argues the structural rise in real yields is likely complete and prefers buying dips in a 4.90%-5.25% range to selling rallies. A Democratic sweep could raise regulatory fears about the AI buildout and slow AI-related issuance and lending, which would ease pressure on long yields. Natixis does not expect an immediate UST rally.

Brazil: Lula won the election with 51.79% of the vote. Fiscal responsibility was the main concern for 76% of surveyed clients. Legislative opposition and US trade or diplomatic pressure are possible, and BRL depends on BCB intervention and the fiscal plans.

Chile: the BCCh tone was hawkish, but Natixis expects the policy rate to stay at 4.50% through 2026 and H1 2027, with the first hike in H2 2027 or 2028. Growth is near 0% in 2026 and unemployment is 9.4%.

Colombia: Natixis expects BanRep to pause at the October 30 meeting, after the September hike to 12.25%. It expects a final hike in December to 12.50%, with low conviction. Inflation is above 6% while activity is contracting.

tension_points.bull_case: Natixis sees the structural rise in real yields as likely complete. A Democratic sweep could raise AI-buildout regulatory fears and slow AI-related issuance and lending, easing pressure on long yields, so it prefers buying dips in the 4.90%-5.25% range.
tension_points.bear_case: AI-related activity has weighed on Treasuries all year, and markets expect it to accelerate next year. Trump holds veto power and supports the buildout, so major federal legislation is unlikely.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yields breaking above the 5.25% top of the expected range.
